title: Gym membership advisor
tagline: Learn to handle the real objections people raise when they consider joining a gym.
you_are: a membership consultant at a mid-size health club
setting: Conversations happen on the gym floor, by phone follow-up, and at the front desk during walk-in enquiries.

scenarios.label: Walk-in tour and trial close
scenarios.desc: A first-time visitor tours the club and you ask for the trial signup.
scenarios.setup: You are the membership consultant. The prospect is a 32-year-old office worker who has never joined a gym. They say: Hi, I just walked in to see what you have.
scenarios.objective: Book a three-day trial that starts this week.
scenarios.moment: Tuesday 6:15 pm, upbeat music from the studio

scenarios.label: Phone follow-up after trial
scenarios.desc: Call a trial user who liked the club but has not converted.
scenarios.setup: You are the membership consultant. The prospect is a 29-year-old teacher who used the three-day trial. They answer: Hello, this is Maya.
scenarios.objective: Secure a twelve-month commitment on the call.

scenarios.label: Corporate referral with spouse objection
scenarios.desc: A company-referred prospect wants the corporate rate but must ask their spouse.
scenarios.setup: You are the membership consultant. The prospect is a 38-year-old engineer sent by HR. They say: My company gets a discount, but I need to run it by my wife first.
scenarios.skills: Value framing and joint decision close
scenarios.objective: Arrange a joint visit or video call with the spouse this week.

buyers.angle: Concern about fitting workouts around kids schedule.
Uses gym app on phone instead of membership.
Demands personal trainer and strict schedule.
Needs low impact exercises and medical clearance.

objections: I need to check with my spouse
I don’t know how to use gym equipment
I’ve tried gyms before and quit
I feel self conscious working out around others
I don’t want to sign a long term contract

rubric.label: Discovery
rubric.what: Ask open questions that reveal the prospect’s goals, schedule, and past barriers before pitching.

rubric.label: Objection handling
rubric.what: Acknowledge each concern, reframe it with a specific club feature, and confirm the prospect feels heard.

rubric.label: Value framing
rubric.what: Translate price into cost per visit, included classes, and health outcomes rather than a monthly fee alone.

rubric.label: Trial close
rubric.what: Propose a concrete trial start date, explain what the trial includes, and ask for the commitment to attend.

rubric.label: Urgency building
rubric.what: Use a real deadline or limited spot to justify deciding now without fabricating scarcity.

rubric.label: Compliance
rubric.what: Disclose contract length, freeze policy, and cancellation terms accurately before any payment detail.

pitfalls: Quoting a monthly price without explaining the annual commitment or freeze rules.
Promising results the club cannot guarantee.
Skipping the spouse conversation and hoping the prospect signs alone.

research.text: Common objections when selling gym memberships include concerns about time, commitment, and ability to use equipment. To address the "I need to check with my spouse" objection, emphasize the importance of personal commitment and ask about their current spending on other fitness-related services. For the "I don’t have time" objection, reframe around flexibility and offer solutions like convenient time slots or virtual workouts. To handle the "I don’t know how to use gym equipment" objection, assure the prospect that you understand their concerns and offer to provide necessary training or resources. The sources suggest that handling objections effectively involves understanding the prospect’s concerns and offering tailored solutions that demonstrate value and commitment.
